units.source: List View
units.context: List View

units.source: List view is similar to __TRILIUM_PH_0__Grid View__TRILIUM_PH_1__, but in the list view mode, each note is displayed in a single row with only the title and the icon of the note being visible by the default. By pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ expand button it's possible to view the content of the note, as well as the children of the note (recursively).
units.context: List View

units.source: In the example above, the "Node.js" note on the left panel contains several child notes. The right panel displays the content of these child notes as a single continuous document.
units.context: List View

units.source: Creating a new table__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: List View > Creating a new table

units.source: Right click on an existing note in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Collection__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__List View__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
units.context: List View > Creating a new table

units.source: Interaction__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: List View > Interaction

units.source: Each note can be expanded or collapsed by clicking on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ arrow to the left of the title.
units.context: List View > Interaction

units.source: In the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ toolbar, the buttons at the right end expand (__TRILIUM_PH_2__) and collapse (__TRILIUM_PH_3__) all notes easily.
units.context: List View > Interaction

units.source: Printing and exporting to PDF__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: List View > Printing and exporting to PDF

units.source: Since v0.100.0, list collections can be __TRILIUM_PH_0__printed or exported to PDF__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: List View > Printing and exporting to PDF

units.source: A printed list collection will print all the notes in the collection, in the right order and preserving the full hierarchy.
units.context: List View > Printing and exporting to PDF

units.source: If exported to PDF within the desktop application, there is additional functionality:
units.context: List View > Printing and exporting to PDF

units.source: The table of contents of the PDF will reflect the structure of the notes.
units.context: List View > Printing and exporting to PDF

units.source: Reference and inline links to other notes within the same hierarchy will be functional (will jump to the corresponding page). If a link refers to a note that is not in the printed hierarchy, it will be unlinked.
units.context: List View > Printing and exporting to PDF

units.source: Expanding and collapsing multiple notes at once__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: List View > Expanding and collapsing multiple notes at once

units.source: Apart from individually expanding or collapsing notes, it's also possible to expand or collapse them all at once. To do so, go to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ toolbar and look for the buttons at its right end.
units.context: List View > Expanding and collapsing multiple notes at once

units.source: By default, the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button expands only the direct children (first level) of the collection. Starting with v0.100.0, it's possible to expand multiple levels of notes using the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ button next to it.
units.context: List View > Expanding and collapsing multiple notes at once

units.source: Manually expanded notes will reset if the application/tab is closed and then the collection is visited again. However notes automatically expanded/collapsed via the buttons in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__ will persist.
units.context: List View > Expanding and collapsing multiple notes at once

units.source: By design, the UI provides only a handful of levels of depth for expanding notes (direct children, 2-5, all levels). It's also possible to specify any desired depth by manually setting the __TRILIUM_PH_0__corresponding label__TRILIUM_PH_1__. For example: __TRILIUM_PH_2__ to expand up to 100 levels of depth.
units.context: List View > Expanding and collapsing multiple notes at once

units.source: From a performance standpoint, the List collection is efficient since it does not load child notes unless the notes are actually expanded. Expanding the list for a significantly large hierarchy can cause slow-downs.
units.context: List View > Expanding and collapsing multiple notes at once
